title: Muuyawkatsina - Moon Spirit
description:
Illustration of Muuyawu, a Kachina moon spirit of the Hopi People of Southern Arizona - widely considered one of the oldest living cultures in the world. Originally by Gerald 
    Dawavendewa (Hopi & Cherokee).
process:
Started with a pencil sketch of the figure and traced over that with fine liners of different weights. Red circle made with acrylic, painted flat and left to dry. It was a joy to 
    try and find the perfect shade by mixing and experimenting.
inspiration: Hopi culture and their Kachina dolls. I just loved the expression of the figure, reminiscent of a traveller of the nights.
meaning: Something about being watched over at night by an entity that slightly unsettles you. The figure isn't doing anything — just being present, looking into you.

title: Taawakatsina - Sun Spirit
description: My reimagination of Taawa, the sun spirit of the Hopi People regarded as the creator of the First World and a guide through existance. Often associated with fertility, life and growth.
process: Rough pencil sketch traced on with fine liners. Used different hatching techniques to create visual somplexity and depth. I chose a lush deep green to represent the sun.
inspiration: Hopi culture and their Kachina dolls. They usually have feline features and the sun spirit looked particularly playful just floating around
meaning: To me, they respresent the will of life, radiating out.
